title: Fixed phrases in conversation
subtitle: I've no idea, no way, in that case
summary: Learn the short fixed phrases English speakers use to answer, to show surprise and to keep a conversation going.

lesson.heading: Common responses
lesson.text: A lot of fixed phrases are used as short answers in everyday conversation. Learn them as whole phrases: you cannot change the words inside them.

examples.text: *A:* What time did he get here? *B:* **I've no idea.**

examples.note: = I'm not sure, because other things affect my answer. Also It depends.

examples.text: *A:* Shall we go out tonight? *B:* Yeah, **why not**?
*A:* Did you like the film? *B:* **Not really.**
*A:* Jason has grown a beard. *B:* **I suppose so.**

lesson.heading: The phrases and what they mean
rows: I'm not sure; other things affect my answer.
No, but I'm not saying it strongly.
Yes, but I'm not saying it strongly.

lesson.heading: Showing surprise
lesson.text: When someone tells you something surprising, say **you must be joking** (also **you're joking** or **you're kidding**). The surprise can be bad or good. If the surprise was something you saw, say **I couldn't believe my eyes**.

examples.text: *A:* We have to work tonight. *B:* **You must be joking.**
*A:* My father said he would pay for all of us to go on holiday. *B:* **You're kidding.** Fantastic!
*A:* Eli got top marks. *B:* I know. **I couldn't believe my eyes!**
examples.note: = I was very surprised when I saw it

lesson.heading: Phrases inside a conversation
lesson.text: These phrases hold a conversation together. **You know** fills a pause. **In that case** means because of the situation you have just described. **Let's wait and see** means wait and find out what happens.

examples.text: I had to **have a word with** Vince and Milan today.
examples.note: = speak to them without other people listening

examples.text: They just keep talking and they don't **pay attention**.
Well, **in that case**, you'll have to move one of them.
I'd **feel bad about** that. They're quite nice boys.

lesson.heading: Asking and deciding
lesson.text: **What if ...?** asks what you will do if something happens. **Change your mind** means change your decision.

examples.note: = what will you do if they don't improve?

examples.text: If you **change your mind**, come and see me again.
Are you still planning to sell the flat? No, I've **changed my mind**.

lesson.heading: sort and kind in informal speech
rows: I grow onions and carrots - that sort of thing.
Her new top is sort of blue.
Well, it was quite difficult, you know.

lesson.text: Learn these phrases as one piece of language. Say *I've no idea*, not ~~I have no the idea~~, and *It depends on the weather*, not ~~It depends of the weather~~.

exercises.prompt: Does the response mean yes, does it mean no, or is the speaker unsure or surprised?
Match each fixed phrase with its meaning.

pairs.right: Because of the situation you describe ...
I was very surprised when I saw it.
Speak to them without others listening.

exercises.prompt: Little children shout and scream all the time; they can't ___ it.
exercises.explanation: Can't help it = can't control some behaviour.

exercises.prompt: *A:* I went to Cambridge last week. *B:* Really? ___ for?
exercises.explanation: The fixed phrase is What for? It means why?

exercises.prompt: The trouble with Mark is that he doesn't ___ attention.
I don't know what they plan to do; we'll have to wait and ___.
exercises.explanation: Wait and see = wait to discover what will happen.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Did you speak to Nathalie? *B:* Yes, I ___ her.
exercises.explanation: Have a word with someone = speak to them privately.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Dad wasn't happy about forgetting my birthday. *B:* No, he felt ___ that.
exercises.explanation: Feel bad about something = be unhappy about it.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Do you know what time he'll be here? *B:* No, I'm afraid I've ___.
exercises.explanation: I've no idea = I don't know.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Are you still planning to sell the flat? *B:* No, I've ___. I'm going to keep it now.
exercises.explanation: Change your mind = change your decision.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Jerry says we'll have to walk all the way to the campsite. *B:* You must be ___! That's ten miles!
exercises.explanation: You must be joking / you're kidding shows that something is a big surprise.

exercises.prompt: *A:* What do they sell? Put B's answer in order.
exercises.answer: Oh, burgers, pizzas, that sort of thing.
alternatives: Oh, burgers, pizzas, that kind of thing.
exercises.explanation: That sort/kind of thing = other examples of the same type.

exercises.statement: *A:* What colour was it? *B:* Kind of blue. - This means the colour was more or less blue.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Kind of / sort of before an adjective means approximately.

exercises.statement: You are not sure about tonight because it depends on your work. You say: 'It depends of my work.'
exercises.explanation: It depends on my work. We say depend on, never depend of.
